---
title: "Lesson 3: Cotangent Spaces"
---

## Overview

Cotangent spaces are the dual spaces to tangent spaces and play a central role in differential forms and calculus on manifolds.

## Intuition

While tangent vectors represent directions, cotangent vectors represent linear measurements of those directions.

## Formal Definition

The cotangent space at $p$ is the dual vector space

$$
T_p^*M = \operatorname{Hom}(T_pM, \mathbb{R}).
$$

A differential $df$ at a point is an example of a cotangent vector.

## Examples

- The differential of a function $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$
- The gradient as a covector in a coordinate formulation
- The role of cotangent spaces in differential geometry
